items.title: Hal Galper interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 27, 2022
items.q: I studied Schillinger so I have an analytical mind. ... I realized how much Schillinger had affected my outlook

ctx.x: When you’re working on a composition over a length of time can I envision sheets of score paper with lines written out in chord symbols or is that not the way you work?

Melody first. I used to write harmony first but the melodies just came out very stilted. You have to do melody first. Once you’ve got the melody then I use something called good note theory, you know, which is: is this note going to be a natural 9 or a flat 9 or is it going to be a fifth of a chord. You know. So I will try it as different functions of different chords to see which sound I was looking for. Look I studied Schillinger so I have an analytical mind. You know. I took Schillinger for two years, that…

you know, because I had Schillinger. And that was a major, the two most important classes were that class and Bob Sher’s re-harmonization class which was re-harmonizing the American songbook from the ukulele changes into jazz changes. Fabulous course. I took to that like a duck to water. My nickname in Boston eventually was the “change master.” Because I could put changes to anything.
